haiku-low.q1: It writes the order as PENDING plus an OrderPlaced outbox row in one transaction. The customer gets 202 Accepted with the order ID before other services act.
haiku-low.q2: The relay marks a row sent only after the broker acknowledges it. If it crashes after the ack but before marking, it resends the row, so duplicates can occur.
haiku-low.q3: Every event is keyed by order ID, so one order's events stay in order, and each consumer group receives them in publish order.
haiku-low.q4: A StockReserved event triggers Payment to charge the card. Inventory publishes it only after reserving stock, so no reservation means no charge.
haiku-low.q5: They write the result event to their outbox in the same transaction as the state change, and the relay publishes it. A crash after commit leaves an unsent row, which the relay still publishes.
haiku-low.q6: Each consumer logs handled eventIds in its own database, in the same transaction as its change. A repeated event finds its eventId in the log and does nothing.
haiku-low.q7: Payment uses the StockReserved eventId as the idempotency key, so the card provider returns the first result without charging again. Payment also logs the eventId.
haiku-low.q8: A decline is a normal answer that leads to cancellation and stock release. A provider timeout or 5xx is an error: the handler throws and retries after 1s, 10s and 60s.
haiku-low.q9: Payment writes PaymentDeclined. Inventory consumes that event and releases the reservation it made earlier.
haiku-low.q10: Order Service reads StockUnavailable, PaymentCaptured or PaymentDeclined events; it never asks services directly. It sets CONFIRMED or CANCELLED and writes OrderConfirmed or OrderCancelled to its outbox.
haiku-low.q11: Notification sends the email after reading OrderConfirmed or OrderCancelled. If sending fails, the order status does not change, because email is best-effort.
haiku-low.q12: Four attempts total: the first, then retries after 1s, 10s and 60s. After the fourth failure the message goes to the group's DLQ, on-call is paged, and the order keeps its status.

sonnet.q1: It writes the order with status PENDING and an OrderPlaced row in its outbox, both in one transaction. It returns 202 Accepted with the order ID, without talking to the broker.
sonnet.q2: The relay marks a row sent only after the broker acknowledges the publish. If it crashes after the ack but before marking the row sent, it sends the row again, so a duplicate event can arrive. Consumers handle this through their eventId log.
sonnet.q3: Every event is keyed by order ID on the topic order-events. So all events for one order stay in order, and each consumer group receives them in the order they were published.
sonnet.q4: Payment charges the card when it reads a StockReserved event. Inventory publishes StockReserved only after reserving stock. If stock is unavailable, Inventory writes StockUnavailable, makes no reservation, and no charge happens. So the card is never charged unless stock is reserved first.
sonnet.q5: Each writes its result event (StockReserved/StockUnavailable, PaymentCaptured/PaymentDeclined) into its own outbox in the same transaction as its state change. The relay then publishes it. A service never publishes directly. If it crashes after committing, the outbox row already exists, and the relay publishes it later (the document says the event exists if and only if the change does). The document does not describe the crash case more explicitly than that.
sonnet.q6: Each consumer logs the eventId of every event it has handled in its own database, in the same transaction as its change. On a repeat it finds the eventId in the log and does nothing. Order Service does the same, so a repeated PaymentCaptured does not write a second OrderConfirmed. Notification logs sent emails by eventId, and Payment also uses an idempotency key.
sonnet.q7: Payment uses the StockReserved eventId as the idempotency key on the charge. The retry sends the same key, so the card provider returns the first result and does not charge again. Payment also logs the eventId, so it never charges twice for the same reservation.
sonnet.q8: A decline is a normal answer. Payment writes PaymentDeclined, which leads to Cancellation 2: the reservation is released and the order is cancelled. A timeout or 5xx is an error, not a decline. The handler throws, and the consumer retries after 1 s, 10 s and 60 s with the same idempotency key. If the fourth attempt fails, the message goes to the DLQ and on-call is paged.
sonnet.q9: The PaymentDeclined event causes the release. Inventory reads PaymentDeclined and releases the reservation, so Inventory is the service that releases it.
sonnet.q10: It learns the outcome from events published by Inventory and Payment, and never asks them directly. On PaymentCaptured it sets the status to CONFIRMED and writes OrderConfirmed to its outbox. On StockUnavailable or PaymentDeclined it sets the status to CANCELLED and writes OrderCancelled to its outbox. Each is done in one transaction.
sonnet.q11: Notification sends the confirmation email when it reads OrderConfirmed, and the cancellation email when it reads OrderCancelled. If the send fails, the order status does not change, because email is best-effort and never an input to any order decision.
sonnet.q12: There are four attempts: the first plus three retries, after 1 s, 10 s and 60 s. The consumer stays on that message while it retries. After the fourth failure the message goes to that consumer group's DLQ, on-call is paged, and the consumer moves on to the next message. Nothing else is undone. The order keeps whatever status it has, for example PENDING, and on-call decides what to do.
